findings.fix: add a TestLoadFragment in internal/config/config_test.go (or installenv_test.go) covering missing-file-empty-settings and malformed-JSON-after-marker-expansion, mirroring the existing TestLoadSave cases for Load.
findings.claim: LoadFragment (internal/config/config.go:212-225) is new core logic — it reads a file, expands install markers, and unmarshals into Settings — but it has no dedicated unit test. internal/config/config_test.go tests Load/Save exhaustively (missing-file, malformed-json, decode errors) and internal/config/installenv_test.go tests only the standalone ExpandInstallMarkers helper; neither exercises LoadFragment itself, so its missing-file branch and its json.Unmarshal failure path (a fragment whose expanded content is malformed JSON) are untested. LoadFragment is called from 4 call sites in internal/server (config.go, config_sync.go, hooks.go, permissions.go), so a regression in its error handling (e.g. silently swallowing a real read error as missing-file, or panicking differently than Load on a malformed fragment) would reach every one of those paths without a failing test catching it.
findings.evidence: Re-read internal/config/config.go:210-225 (LoadFragment) and internal/config/config_test.go in full: TestLoadSave only calls Load, never LoadFragment; TestFileIOErrors/TestSettingsDecodeErrors likewise target Load's typed views, not LoadFragment. Re-read internal/config/installenv_test.go in full: TestExpandInstallMarkers covers only the marker-substitution function, called with raw []byte literals, never through LoadFragment's os.ReadFile + json.Unmarshal wrapper. grep -n "LoadFragment" across internal/*.go confirms 4 server call sites and zero test references. The claim survives: no test in my assigned files exercises LoadFragment directly.

findings.fix: add a build-tagged sched_windows_test.go (or extend an existing Windows-only test file) covering SyncAll's new `state == "NotFound" && routine.DefaultDisabled` skip branch, at minimum by extracting the branch condition into a small pure helper that a platform-agnostic test can call.
findings.claim: sched_windows.go's SyncAll gained a new condition at line 157 (`if state == "NotFound" && routine.DefaultDisabled { ... continue }`) mirroring the darwin default-disabled gating added in the same change, but `internal/routines/` has no sched_windows_test.go or any other `//go:build windows` test file — `git ls-files internal/routines/` lists bootstrap_darwin.go, launchctl_darwin.go, launchctl_darwin_test.go, plist.go, plist_test.go, routines.go, routines_test.go, sched_other.go, sched_windows.go, taskxml.go, taskxml_test.go, tokens.go, tokens_test.go: taskxml_test.go exists for the neighboring Windows-only taskxml.go, but nothing tests sched_windows.go's functions (taskState, IsLoaded, Start, SyncAll) at all, old or new. The new default-disabled skip is therefore added to an already-zero-coverage file, with no test asserting it actually prevents Start from firing when a routine is both unregistered and default-disabled.
findings.evidence: Re-ran `git ls-files internal/routines/` in the lane worktree and confirmed no sched_windows_test.go or other file matching `_windows_test.go` exists; re-read sched_windows.go in full (the new branch at line 157-160) and confirmed SyncAll's only test-adjacent sibling is taskxml_test.go, which does not reference SyncAll, taskState, or DefaultDisabled. The gap is real and the new branch adds to it.

findings.fix: none — functionally covered; optionally rename the "reserved-name-fails" subtest's enclosing context or add a one-line comment cross-referencing the spec so the next reader can find it by the name spec-8 uses.
findings.claim: spec-8-change-bootstrap-profile.md's test table names a test `internal/repos/registry_test.go TestRepoValidate` with cases "reserved names rejected, existing name rules still pass", but no function named TestRepoValidate exists in registry_test.go. The equivalent cases are instead covered by the "reserved-name-fails" subtest inside TestRegistryAdd (line 87-95), alongside the pre-existing "invalid-name-fails" and "relative-path-fails" subtests of the same function, which together cover both the new reserved-name rule and the existing Validate rules in substance. This is a named-vs-actual test mismatch, not a coverage gap: every case the spec lists is exercised, just under a different test function name than the spec specifies.
findings.evidence: Re-read spec-8-change-bootstrap-profile.md line 752 verbatim (quoted in the claim) and re-ran `git grep -n "func Test" internal/repos/registry_test.go` in the lane worktree, which lists TestRegistryAdd but no TestRepoValidate anywhere in the file. Re-read TestRegistryAdd in full (lines 53-114) and confirmed its "reserved-name-fails", "invalid-name-fails", and "relative-path-fails" subtests jointly exercise every Validate rule, including the new reserved-name check added by this diff. The naming mismatch is real; the functional coverage is not missing.

notes: cmd/acdsl/verifiers/planformat/main.go's canon reorder has no Go unit test, but this repo's own convention tests verifiers through acdsl fixtures (acdsl/testdata/<rule-id>/pass|fail), not Go *_test.go files — testdata/ACDSL-PLAN-001/pass/plan.md changed in the same commit (visible in the full diff, outside my go-core chunk), so this is covered by the project's established mechanism, not a gap. internal/repos/registry.go's Add/Remove read-modify-write race (external write between snapshot read and save) is held safely by r.mu for the whole critical section in-process; TestRegistryDeleteStaysDeletedAcrossInstances documents the only real race (two separate Registry instances, i.e. two OS processes) and is itself a cross-chunk concern (server lifecycle), flagged here only as a note, not a finding, since no evidence shows it reaches two processes in this repo's actual usage. No BLOCKER/MAJOR findings from this chunk; the three MINOR/NIT findings are coverage-naming gaps, not functional defects.
